recommendation: Keep the commit. It corrects implementation defects in the already-accepted FHIR-20972 change without expanding into later unresolved Account.balance design questions; handle aggregate wording or coverage-specific attribution under their own future applied Jira decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-20972 asked to add balance back to Account so servers can expose balance information without requiring extra calls; the Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution added Account.balance 0..* with aggregate, term, estimate, amount, and calculatedAt.
initial_application: Commit 4929a4c049aed8232988ff0619032aa5c694af73 added the Account.balance backbone and the aggregate/balance-term terminology for R5. Current source already had the requested elements, but Account.balance.calculatedAt had the wrong ElementDefinition.path, Account narrative still described direct balance as future work, and AccountBalanceTerm pointed to the wrong value set URL.
additional_context: Account is active in source/fhir.ini. The linked Zulip thread and PA/FM Confluence minutes preserve the concern that balances are volatile while confirming acceptance of reintroducing a balance concept with a timestamp. Later FHIR-53831 and FHIR-53832 concern separate future Account.balance refinements and were not final Applied/Published source-edit decisions for this run.
reconciliation: Changed Account.balance.calculatedAt path to Account.balance.calculatedAt, updated Account scope text to describe optional calculated balances, corrected the AccountBalanceTerm CodeSystem.valueSet to account-balance-term, and aligned the checked-in Account SVG so calculatedAt appears under balance.

source/account/account-introduction.xml: replaced stale operation-only/future-work wording with optional calculated-balance guidance consistent with Account.balance.
source/account/codesystem-account-balance-term.xml: corrected CodeSystem.valueSet from account-payment-terms to account-balance-term.
source/account/account.svg: moved calculatedAt from top-level Account display into the Balance backbone display and linked it to Account.balance.calculatedAt.
